items.followUp: What is meant by problem solving?

rubric.why: A problem is a situation that presents a challenge or difficulty.
rubric.description: Identifies a challenging situation or difficulty.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that a problem is a situation, challenge, or difficulty.

rubric.description: States that the situation requires a solution.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning that a solution is needed.

modelAnswer: A problem is a situation or difficulty that presents a challenge.

items.followUp: Differentiate between a web page and a website.

rubric.why: The anchor tag is the HTML element used to create a link.
rubric.description: Identifies the anchor as the HTML tag used to create a link.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying the anchor tag, such as <a>.

rubric.why: A hyperlink is the clickable connection that leads to another page, resource, or location.
rubric.description: Explains what a hyperlink does or where it leads.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing a hyperlink as a clickable link to another page, resource, or location.

modelAnswer: The <a> (anchor) tag is used in HTML to create a link.
A hyperlink is the clickable text or image that takes the user to another webpage, resource, or location.

items.followUp: What is the purpose of the <u> and <strong> tags in HTML?

rubric.why: The <i> tag displays text in italic style.
rubric.description: States the purpose of the <i> tag.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for saying that <i> makes text italic.

rubric.why: The <b> tag displays text in bold style.
rubric.description: States the purpose of the <b> tag.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for saying that <b> makes text bold.

modelAnswer: The <i> tag displays text in italic style.
The <b> tag displays text in bold style.

items.followUp: What digits are used in the binary number system, and what is its base?

rubric.why: The binary number system uses only the digits 0 and 1.
rubric.description: Names the digits used in binary.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both 0 and 1.

rubric.why: Binary is a positional number system with base 2.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for giving its base as 2.

modelAnswer: The binary number system uses only the digits 0 and 1.

items.followUp: What does the AND operator return when both inputs are true?

rubric.why: NOT is a unary logical operator that performs negation.
rubric.description: Identifies NOT as a logical negation operator.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as a logical negation or unary operator.

rubric.why: NOT reverses the truth value of its input.
rubric.description: Explains that NOT changes true to false and false to true.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that it reverses the truth value.

modelAnswer: The NOT operator is a unary logical operator that negates its input.
It reverses the truth value: true becomes false and false becomes true.

rubric.why: Volatile memory loses its stored data when power is turned off.
rubric.description: Describes what happens to volatile memory without power.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that volatile memory loses data when power is off.

rubric.why: Non-volatile memory retains its data even when power is turned off.
rubric.description: Describes what happens to non-volatile memory without power.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that non-volatile memory retains data without power.

modelAnswer: Volatile memory loses its data when the power is turned off.
Non-volatile memory retains its data even when the power is turned off.

items.followUp: What is data security, and how does it help protect information?

rubric.why: Data privacy concerns protecting personal or private information.
rubric.description: Identifies the information that data privacy protects.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for referring to personal, private, or sensitive information.

rubric.why: Data privacy protects information from unauthorized access or use.
rubric.description: Explains the protection provided by data privacy.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for mentioning protection from unauthorized access or use.

modelAnswer: Data privacy is the protection of personal or private information.
It prevents unauthorized access to or use of that information.

items.followUp: What is the World Wide Web, and how is it related to the Internet?

rubric.why: The Internet is a global network of interconnected computer networks.
rubric.description: Describes the Internet as a global network of connected networks.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for describing it as a worldwide or global network of interconnected networks.

rubric.why: The Internet connects computers or computer networks around the world.
rubric.description: Identifies what is connected through the Internet.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating that computers or computer networks are connected.

modelAnswer: The Internet is a global network of interconnected computer networks.
It connects computers around the world and enables them to communicate and share information.
